claim_verdicts.evidence: Key shell fits. Bash 5.3 manual 3.7.3: a simple command 'is invoked in a separate execution environment that consists of ... The shell's open files, plus any modifications and additions specified by redirections to the command.' 3.6.1/3.6.2 name 'the standard input (file descriptor 0)' and 'the standard output (file descriptor 1)'. Prior execution r2 (lab box): `ls -l /proc/self/fd | cat` lists fds 0, 1, 2 for `ls`, which never reads stdin.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Key shell fits. Bash 5.3 manual 3.7.3: the command inherits 'The shell's open files' unless redirections change them, so with no redirection fds 1 and 2 are the shell's, i.e. the terminal in an interactive session. Prior execution r2: with -t, fds 0/2 -> /dev/pts/0; `ls /nowhere /repo/lab` printed the error in the same column as the listing.
claim_verdicts.source: gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html (Edition 5.3), 3.7.3 Command Execution Environment; execution r2 2026-09-27 donhang-lab

claim_verdicts.evidence: Key shell fits. Bash 5.3 manual 3.2.3 Pipelines: 'The output of each command in the pipeline is connected via a pipe to the input of the next command. That is, each command reads the previous command's output.' Prior execution r2: `ls -l /proc/self/fd | cat` shows `1 -> pipe:[14836311]`, no path on disk.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Key shell fits the concurrency half. Bash 5.3 manual 3.2.3: 'Each command in a multi-command pipeline, where pipes are created, is executed in its own subshell, which is a separate process' and 'the shell waits for all commands in the pipeline to complete'; 'concurrently' is not used, so the decisive evidence is execution r2 in the lab box with BusyBox 1.37 grep: `time (yes ERROR | grep ERROR | head -3)` printed three lines, real 0m0.006s, infinite left side. The 'when matches are frequent' hedge does not depend on GNU grep.
claim_verdicts.source: gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html (Edition 5.3), 3.2.3 Pipelines; execution r2 2026-09-27 donhang-lab (bash 5.3.9, BusyBox grep)
